To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collagen hydrolysates from jumbo squid arms showed the highest antioxidant, antimutagens and antiproliferrative activities.
collagen hydrolysates from jumbo squid arms and fins, produced by trypsis and protease XIV had different antioxidant, antimutagent and antiproliferaive activities.

the jumbo squid byproduct hydrolysates have the potential to be developed as natural antioxidants, antimutagens and/or antiproliferatives, and the collagen hydrolysates obtained from jumbo squid by-products could have a potential use in the food, pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valorization of jumbo squid by-products and their potential use in the development of food products with antioxidant properties and antimutagenic potential.
the valorization of jumbo squid byproduct, which is currently wasted, by the development of a new functional ingredient.
obtaining new bioactive peptides from byproducts, which could be used as functional food ingredients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
jumbo squid arm collagen hydrolysates have the best potential to be applied as functional food additives.
jumbo squid arm hydrolysates have higher potential to be applied as natural antioxidant and antimutagenic food additives.
the jumbo squid byproduct hydrolysates have potential to be used as food additives, however, further research is needed to determine its application in food industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrolysates of collagen from jumbo squid arms are promising sources of bioactive peptides, with antioxidant, antimutagentic and antiprolificative activities.
jumbo squid arm collagen hydrolysate produced by protease type XIV has the potential to be applied as antioxidant, antimutagens and antiproliferrative agent in food industry.
the hydrolysates obtained from the jumbo squid by-products are promising sources of bioactive peptides that may be used as food additives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collagen hydrolysates obtained from jumbo squid by-products could have potential applications as functional foods and as nutraceuticals.
the jumbo squid byproduct-derived hydrolysates are a good source of bioactive peptides that may contribute to human health.
collagen hydrolysates obtained from byproducts of jumbo squid can be used as functional ingredients with antioxidant, antimutagent and antiproliterative activity.
